findings.quote: Consensus expects revenue to grow to $138.6M in FY27E with EPS of $0.23, and to $157.2M in FY28E with EPS of $0.32, which would mark a return to GAAP profitability.
findings.issue: The consensus EPS estimates ($0.23 FY27E, $0.32 FY28E) are quoted correctly, but nothing on the grounding surface labels them GAAP or non-GAAP; the Facts estimates block gives 'EPS $0.23 / $0.32' with no basis. The press release states EPS guidance is 'provided only on a non-GAAP basis,' and the company already prints positive non-GAAP EPS ($0.15 in FY26). Asserting the estimate 'would mark a return to GAAP profitability' presupposes a GAAP basis the pack does not establish. The same GAAP-return framing recurs as 'a return to positive EPS' in analystCommentary, executiveSummary.catalysts[0], growth.points[5] and finalRecommendation.body[0]; if the estimates are non-GAAP, the 'return' framing is wrong because non-GAAP EPS is already positive. This is the report's thesis-carrying profitability-inflection claim.
findings.fix: Drop the word 'GAAP', or state that the consensus EPS basis is not labelled in the pack. Frame it as consensus modelling positive EPS ($0.23/$0.32) versus the FY26 GAAP loss of $-0.10, without asserting the estimate itself is GAAP. Apply the same hedge everywhere the 'return to positive EPS / profitability' framing appears.
findings.note: Re-verified after the rewrite. Still resolved: no 'return to GAAP profitability' framing remains, and the report says the pack does not label the consensus EPS as GAAP or non-GAAP (that hedge now recurs too often; see F-20).

findings.quote: Gross margin for the consolidated business was 43.8% in FY26.
findings.issue: Load-bearing figures are restated rather than introduced once and referred back in words (rubric 7). Gross margin 43.8% appears three times inside the businessMoat section alone: segments[0].body ('Gross margin for the consolidated business was 43.8% in FY26'), moatFactors[2] Pricing power ('Gross margin improved to 43.8% in FY26, but operating margin was still -3.4%') and durability ('Gross margin of 43.8% and a net cash balance sheet...'); it recurs about seven times report-wide. The Nero acquisition economics ($5.3M annual revenue / $4.5M ARR) are restated in full in catalysts[2], growth.points[3] and capitalAllocation, and the 'Software and Services above 10% on a pro forma basis' claim appears in catalysts[2], growth.points[3], segments[0].body and durability. FY27E $138.6M / $0.23 likewise recurs across analystCommentary, thesis, catalysts, valuation, growth and finalRecommendation.
findings.fix: Introduce each figure once in its home section (gross margin in the segment line; Nero economics in either growth or capital allocation, not both; FY27E consensus in valuation) and refer back in words elsewhere ('the same 43.8% margin', 'the acquisition above'). Keep executive-summary catalysts as pointers instead of repeating the full numbers the later sections carry.
findings.note: Re-verified after the rewrite. 43.8% appears once in prose (incomeCommentary), the FY27E/FY28E figures once (growth.points[0], with valuation using the EPS as anchors), and the Nero economics once (growth.points[2]); other sections point in words.

findings.quote: Q4'26 revenue was $31.2M, up 4.6% year over year on the desk's figures; the company's press release described the same quarter as up 8%, and I used the 4.6% figure.
findings.issue: Disclosing the source disagreement (desk +4.6% vs press release +8%) and stating which figure was used is correct (rubric 8). The voice, though, slips into first-person singular ('I used the 4.6% figure') where the rest of the report speaks collectively as 'we' / 'the desk' ('We rate', 'Our target range', 'on the desk's figures' in the same sentence). One inconsistent voice tic.
findings.fix: Recast in the report's collective voice, e.g. 'the desk used the 4.6% figure' or 'we use the 4.6% figure', to match 'We rate' / 'Our target' elsewhere.
findings.note: Re-verified after the rewrite. Still resolved: 'and we use the 4.6% figure'; the disagreement with the release's 8% is stated once and dated to the August 26, 2026 release.

findings.quote: Revenue grows at a double-digit rate toward the FY27E consensus of $138.6M, EPS turns positive at $0.23, and the stock holds a mid-2x sales multiple, landing near the lower half of the Street target range.
findings.issue: The Base implied price is $9.00. On ~46.71M shares that is a ~$420M market cap, which on FY27E revenue of $138.6M is ~3.0x sales, not the 'mid-2x sales multiple' the driver states (a mid-2x multiple on $138.6M would imply roughly $7.4). The stated multiple is internally inconsistent with the $9.00 it is meant to justify; the price is really pegged to the 'lower half of the Street target range' clause, not to the multiple.
findings.fix: Either state ~3x forward sales (consistent with $9.00) or drop the multiple and anchor the base explicitly to the lower half of the Street $8-12 range. Current P/S is 2.4x, so if you keep a sales-multiple anchor, note that the base assumes modest multiple expansion.
findings.note: Re-verified after the rewrite. The Base is now re-anchored to today's 27.0x forward P/E rolled onto FY28E EPS of $0.32 ($8.64), so the sales-multiple inconsistency no longer applies.

findings.quote: We rate Lantronix a BUY with a target range of $8.00 to $11.00 against a $6.25 price, below the Street's $10.25 consensus but above the current quote.
findings.issue: Under today's rating rule the scenarios derive STRONG BUY, not BUY: the weighted fair value of $8.55 against $6.25 gives expected upside of +36.8%, the $5.00 Bear gives bear-case downside of 20.0%, and reward/risk is 1.84x, which clears both STRONG BUY bars (E >= +20.0%, R >= 1.00x). The build records 'author's published label BUY differs from the composed STRONG BUY'. A one-notch-conservative label is allowed, but only if the report says so and says why. The report never states the derived label, never quotes E, D or R, and never explains why it publishes one notch below what its own scenarios derive. A reader sees a BUY whose numbers say STRONG BUY with no explanation (rubric 6).
findings.fix: Either publish the derived STRONG BUY, or keep BUY and say once, in the final recommendation, that the scenarios derive STRONG BUY (quote the expected upside and reward/risk from the calls) and that BUY is a deliberate one-notch-conservative call, with the reason drawn from the page (for example the GAAP losses and the still-declining FY26 revenue). Do not move prices or weights to make the scenarios land on BUY; if the scenarios change after F-6 and F-7, state whatever label they then derive.
findings.note: Resolved. finalRecommendation.body[0] states that the scenarios derive STRONG BUY (+31.9%, 1.06x), publishes BUY as a deliberate one-notch-conservative call, and gives the reasons: a narrow clearance of the 1.00x bar, the sensitivity, and the unlabelled EPS basis. Reviewer arithmetic confirms $8.24, +31.9%, -30.1% and 1.06x.

findings.quote: revenue stays near FY26's $120.9M, GAAP losses persist, and the multiple compresses, taking the stock about 20% below the current $6.25 to $5.00.
findings.issue: The Bear price has no anchor a reader can check. It is defined by its own distance from the price ('about 20% below'), which is circular, and the multiple it 'compresses' to is never named. The 52-week low on the page is $4.37, below the $5.00 Bear, so the stock traded under the Bear price within the past year while the Bear story (flat revenue, continuing GAAP losses, a lower multiple) describes conditions no better than FY26's. The report does not say why the downside should stop above a price the market has already paid. The weights are also asserted rather than argued: scenarioCommentary says only 'We skew the reward to the upside but retain that Bear weight on the case where the turn does not arrive', and nothing argues why Bull deserves 25% or Bear 30% (rubric 5 and 6).
findings.fix: Anchor the Bear to a figure on the page and say the basis, for example a stated sales multiple on FY26 revenue, or the 52-week low, and argue whether the Bear should sit at, above or below that low. Argue the Bear weight on the Bear case itself, and give the Bull weight one sentence of reasoning. If the label moves as a result, state the label the scenarios derive (see F-5).
findings.note: Resolved. The Bear is anchored to the $4.37 52-week low, with an argument for why it sits at that low and not above or below it. Each weight is argued on its own case (Bull 20%, Base 55%, Bear 25%). The sensitivity claims check out: Base to Bear moves R to 0.95x, the sales anchor moves E to +18.5%, and Base to Bull keeps R at 1.15x.

findings.quote: the stock re-rates into the lower half of the Street target range on modest multiple expansion from the current 2.4x sales.
findings.issue: The re-rating the Base needs is not modest. The $9.00 Base is about 44% above the $6.25 price, while consensus revenue grows about 15% into FY27E (Snapshot). On a like-for-like basis the sales multiple therefore has to rise by roughly 25% (about 2.1x to about 3.0x FY27E revenue, reviewer arithmetic; or about 2.4x to about 3.5x on FY26 revenue). On earnings the gap is larger: the page shows a 27.0x NTM P/E at $6.25, and $9.00 on the same $0.23 FY27E EPS is near 39x. Calling that 'modest' understates what the Base, which carries 45% of the weight and most of the label, assumes. The anchor to the lower half of the Street range is checkable, but the report does not argue why the uniformly bullish Street range is the right base (rubric 6).
findings.fix: Drop 'modest' and say in words how large a re-rating the Base requires on both the sales and the earnings basis the page shows, without computing new figures in the prose. Argue from both sides why the stock should earn it (or not) within the target window, and say the anchor is the Street range. Do not quote the reviewer's arithmetic.
findings.note: Resolved. 'Modest' is gone. The Base holds today's forward multiple a year out, which the commentary argues from both sides; it says a clearly higher sales multiple is needed and that the anchor decides the label. Using the high Street target only for the Bull is stated.

findings.quote: the filing gives no product or geographic revenue split, so FY26 revenue of $120.9M is shown as one consolidated line.
findings.issue: Facts and claims are attached to a document that did not carry them (over-attribution; rubric 2). (1) companyOverview says 'the filing gives no product or geographic revenue split', and segments[0].body says 'no product or geographic split disclosed'. The surface says only that 'The vendor breaks out no product or geographic revenue mix', and the MD&A excerpt names three product lines and three sales regions, so nothing shows that the 10-K omits a split. (2) durability says 'a risk factor cites intense competition and resultant downward price pressure'. That phrase comes from the press release's forward-looking-statements list, not the 10-K risk-factor excerpt. (3) risks.systemic says 'The filing cites worsening regional and global economic conditions and their effect on customer purchasing decisions' and 'Rising interest rates and the stability of financial and banking institutions are also named'. These items come from the press release's forward-looking statements; the 10-K excerpt names the conflicts, the Red Sea, China and Taiwan, and the tariffs.
findings.fix: (1) Say that the pack carries no product or geographic revenue split, not that the filing gives none. (2) Attribute the competition and price-pressure phrase to the earnings release's forward-looking statements. (3) Split risks.systemic by source: the 10-K risk factors for the conflicts and the tariffs, and the August 26, 2026 earnings release for economic conditions, interest rates and banking stability.
findings.note: Resolved. companyOverview and segments[0] say the pack, not the filing, carries no split. Pricing power attributes the competition phrase to the release's forward-looking statements. risks.systemic splits the 10-K risk factors from the release's forward-looking statements, and each item matches its source.

findings.field: sections.executiveSummary.thesis.body; executiveSummary.risks[3]; valuation.scenarioCommentary; risks.idiosyncratic[3]; finalRecommendation.body[0]; management.leadership
findings.quote: The counter-case is that FY26 revenue still fell, the company remains unprofitable on a GAAP basis, and the growth thesis leans on defense and government demand that the filing itself flags as uncertain.
findings.issue: The report makes the same claims in many places, in different words (rubric 7). (a) 'FY26 revenue still fell and the company is still GAAP loss-making' is argued six times: thesis (quoted); executiveSummary.risks[3] ('FY26 revenue still declined year over year and the company remained GAAP loss-making'); scenarioCommentary ('FY26 revenue still declined 1.6% and the GAAP result was a loss'); risks.idiosyncratic[3] ('FY26 revenue still fell 1.6% and the company remained GAAP loss-making'); finalRecommendation.body[0] ('was still down 1.6% and the company remained GAAP loss-making at $-0.10 per share'); and leadership ('fell 23.3% in FY25 and 1.6% in FY26, and the company has not produced a GAAP profit'). (b) 'About $60 million of cash and no debt' is restated in analystCommentary, thesis, balanceCommentary and finalRecommendation.body[0]. (c) 'Unmanned systems to 15% to 20% of FY2027 revenue' is restated in analystCommentary, thesis, growth.points[1] and finalRecommendation.body[0]. (d) Outsourced manufacturing in Asia is told in companyOverview, executiveSummary.risks[4] (the lint flags it at 0.62 similarity), moatFactors[3], cashflowCommentary, capitalAllocation and risks.systemic.
findings.fix: Give each claim one home. Put the 'still declining, still loss-making' counter-case in the risks section and point to it elsewhere in words. Put the cash and no-debt figure in balanceCommentary, the 15% to 20% guide in growth, and the Asia manufacturing risk in risks.idiosyncratic. Leave the executive summary and the final recommendation as short pointers, and remove the five-year revenue recap from leadership.
findings.note: Resolved for the claims named. The 'still declining, still loss-making' case lives in risks.idiosyncratic[3], with pointers elsewhere. $60 million appears only in balanceCommentary, 15% to 20% only in growth.points[1], and the Asia manufacturing risk only in risks.idiosyncratic[2]. leadership no longer recaps revenue. New repetition the rewrite introduced is raised as F-20.

findings.quote: The company guides Q1 FY2027 revenue of $31.0 million to $33.0 million.
findings.issue: The growth section is six bullish points with no counter-case (rubric 5). It lists the consensus path, unmanned systems, partnerships, Nero, the SLC 9000 and the Q1 guide, but never names the reading that cuts the other way, even though the page carries it. The low end of the Q1 FY2027 guide ($31.0 million) sits below Q4'26 revenue of $31.2M, so the guide does not rule out a sequential decline after 'five consecutive quarters' of growth. Nero's approximately $5.3 million of annual revenue is small against FY26 revenue of $120.9M. The unmanned-systems ramp depends on government contracts that the 10-K says can be cut, delayed or terminated for convenience. The Q1 guide point is also a bare figure with no view.
findings.fix: Add one counter-case point that uses figures already on the page. For example, say the low end of the Q1 guide sits below the Q4'26 revenue, and that the acquisition's revenue is small relative to the FY26 base. Point to the risks section for the defense-budget dependence instead of restating it. Give the Q1 guide point a view: what it says about the double-digit FY2027 claim.
findings.note: Resolved. growth.points[5] gives three counter-readings from page figures: the low end of the guide sits below Q4'26, the acquired revenue is small against FY26, and it points to the government-contract risk. growth.points[4] gives the Q1 guide a view.

findings.quote: The proxy lists a board that includes James Auker, Sailesh Chittipeddi, and Hoshi Printer as directors, with Narbeh Derhacobian and Kevin Palatnik as director nominees
findings.issue: The board and officer roster comes from the DEF 14A filed September 24, 2025 (ownership measured as of September 8, 2025), about a year before this report, but leadership presents it undated as the current board (rubric 3). 'Director nominees' is a status as of that proxy; the pack does not show whether they were elected or whether the roster has changed since. The governance section dates the proxy, but leadership, where a reader meets the names, does not. Beyond the names, the paragraph's only view is the restated five-year revenue record, which F-9 covers (rubric 4).
findings.fix: Date the roster in leadership ('the September 2025 proxy listed…') and keep 'director nominees' tied to that proxy. Replace the revenue recap with a view on leadership that the surface supports, such as the CEO's stated strategy and what the FY26 results show about delivery on it.
findings.note: Resolved. leadership dates the roster to the DEF 14A filed September 24, 2025, ties the nominees to that year's meeting, says the pack does not show later changes, and replaces the revenue recap with a view on strategy and delivery. The 'beat' wording there is raised as F-19.

findings.quote: The modest insider stake means management's alignment comes more through compensation than through a large founder-sized equity position.
findings.issue: The conclusion rests on pay data the pack does not carry. The governance section itself says 'The proxy excerpt does not carry full board-independence or compensation detail', so 'alignment comes more through compensation' is unsupported. The paragraph also does not read the two large holdings for outside holders (rubric 4). It lists Bernhard Bruscha's 13.8% (mostly through TL Investment GmbH) and Chain of Lakes Group's 7.8% (reported on a Schedule 13D/A filed July 1, 2025) but never says what those blocks mean for other shareholders. A 13.8% holder is a large block but not control, and the two blocks together are far larger than the board-and-management group's 2.4%.
findings.fix: Drop the compensation clause, or say the pack carries no pay detail. Give a view on what the two dated blocks mean for outside holders, such as the influence of a 13.8% holder short of control and the gap between outside blocks and insider ownership. Keep the September 8, 2025 dating.
findings.note: Resolved. The compensation clause now reads 'the pack carries no pay detail'. The section gives a view on the 13.8% block (large, not control) and on outside blocks versus the 2.4% insider stake, with the September 8, 2025 and July 1, 2025 dating kept.

findings.quote: Positive free cash flow alongside a GAAP net loss reflects non-cash charges; the company's non-GAAP reconciliation adds back share-based compensation, depreciation and amortization, and amortization of purchased intangibles, among other items.
findings.issue: This is a causal claim the pack does not establish (rubric 2). The pack has no cash-flow bridge from net loss to operating cash flow, so it cannot show how much of the gap between the -$4.2M net loss and $9.3M of free cash flow comes from non-cash charges and how much from working capital. The press release's list of items 'excluded' from non-GAAP net loss reconciles to non-GAAP earnings, not to cash flow. It also mixes non-cash items with cash items such as interest, taxes, restructuring and acquisition costs, so it cannot serve as evidence for the cash story. Graded Important rather than Critical because no figure is misstated and the sentence does not carry the call.
findings.fix: Hedge the cause. For example: the gap between the net loss and positive free cash flow is consistent with non-cash charges such as share-based compensation and amortization, which the company excludes from its non-GAAP results, but the pack carries no cash-flow bridge, so working capital may also contribute. Do not present the non-GAAP exclusion list as a cash reconciliation.
findings.note: Resolved. The cause is hedged ('is consistent with'), the missing cash-flow bridge and possible working-capital effect are stated, and the report says the non-GAAP list is not a cash reconciliation.

findings.quote: Management described the year-end balance sheet as the strongest in the company's history.
findings.issue: This paraphrase changes what the company claimed. The CEO said 'We enter fiscal 2027 in the strongest financial position in our company's history' and that the company 'significantly strengthened our balance sheet'. 'Strongest financial position' is not 'strongest balance sheet', and where the phrasing carries a superlative, the company's own words should be quoted (rubric 9).
findings.fix: Quote the company's phrase, 'the strongest financial position in our company's history', and attribute it to the CEO in the August 26, 2026 release.
findings.note: Resolved. The CEO's phrase is quoted verbatim and attributed to the August 26, 2026 release.

findings.quote: the current share count is higher, at about 46.71M, so ownership percentages drawn from the proxy predate more recent issuance.
findings.issue: No source on the surface reports an issuance. The Quote line says the 46.71M share count is 'derived from market cap', so the report infers new shares from a vendor-derived figure. The right conclusion is that the proxy's percentages are measured against an older, smaller base and may overstate current stakes, but the cause ('more recent issuance') is an inference the pack does not make.
findings.fix: Say the pack's current share count (about 46.71M, derived from market cap) is above the proxy's 39,271,361 base, so the proxy's percentages may overstate holders' current stakes. Do not name issuance as the cause.
findings.note: Resolved. governance says the share count of about 46.71M is derived from market cap and sits above the proxy's 39,271,361 base, so the proxy's percentages may overstate current stakes. No issuance is asserted.

findings.quote: The company returns no cash to shareholders: no dividend, and no buybacks across the five-year window.
findings.issue: The Share Repurchases row is '—' in every year, which means the figure is not reported in the pack, not zero. The 0.00% dividend yield supports 'no dividend', but nothing on the surface establishes 'no buybacks'. The statement is likely the right reading but is asserted more firmly than the data allows.
findings.fix: Say the pack reports no repurchases in the five-year window and the dividend yield is 0.00%, rather than asserting that no buybacks took place.
findings.note: Resolved. The section now reads 'the pack reports no share repurchases in any of the five years shown', with the 0.00% dividend yield.

findings.quote: Addition to the Russell 3000 Index in the 2026 reconstitution broadens the shareholder base.
findings.issue: The company said the addition reflects its progress and is 'broadening the Company's visibility within the investment community'. 'Broadens the shareholder base' is a stronger effect that the pack does not show. The addition has also already happened in the 2026 reconstitution, so it is a completed event rather than a forward catalyst.
findings.fix: Use the company's phrase, visibility within the investment community, and frame it as a completed event. Alternatively, drop it from the catalysts.
findings.note: Resolved. The Russell 3000 catalyst is removed.

findings.quote: Consensus models double-digit FY27 revenue growth, rising further in FY28E, consistent with the estimates carried in the financials section.
findings.issue: 'Rising further in FY28E' can be read as growth accelerating. FY28E revenue of $157.2M does rise again, but at a slower rate than FY27E's +15%, so the phrase is ambiguous in the direction the thesis prefers.
findings.fix: Say revenue rises again in FY28E, without implying the growth rate rises.
findings.note: Resolved. growth.points[0] reads 'revenue rising again to $157.2M in FY28E'.

findings.quote: The beat on its own outlook is the strongest evidence in the pack that the new engine is real.
findings.issue: Unmanned-systems revenue of $12.6M landed inside the company's $10 million to $14 million outlook. The release says it was 'above the midpoint of the prior guidance range'. Calling that a 'beat on its own outlook' (growth.points[1]), or saying it 'beat the outlook management had given' (leadership), overstates what the source reports: a result inside the range is not a beat of the outlook. The claim does work in the argument. growth calls it 'the strongest evidence in the pack that the new engine is real', and leadership uses it as the proof of 'partial delivery'. scenarioCommentary phrases it correctly ('above the midpoint of its outlook'). This is rubric 2: a characterisation the source does not make.
findings.fix: In both places, use the release's wording: above the midpoint of the $10 million to $14 million outlook. Restate the evidential claim to fit, for example 'landing above the midpoint of its own outlook is the strongest evidence…'. Do not call it a beat.
findings.note: Resolved. growth.points[1] now reads 'Landing above the midpoint of its own outlook is the strongest evidence in the pack…', matching the release's 'above the midpoint'. leadership points to the growth section ('landed where the growth section sets out') instead of calling it a beat.

findings.quote: The case against is that the turn is not yet visible in the full-year GAAP numbers and that the EPS path the Base rests on carries no GAAP or non-GAAP label in the pack.
findings.issue: The rewrite moved one claim into five places (rubric 7). That the consensus EPS has no GAAP or non-GAAP label is stated in the thesis (quoted); in multiplesCommentary ('The pack does not label the consensus EPS as GAAP or non-GAAP'); in the Base driver ('consensus EPS whose GAAP or non-GAAP basis the pack does not label'); in scenarioCommentary ('that multiple sits on EPS of unlabelled basis'); and in finalRecommendation.body[0] ('The Base also rests on consensus EPS of unlabelled basis'). Smaller repeats were also introduced. The above-midpoint unmanned result is used as evidence in growth.points[1], leadership and scenarioCommentary. 'The low end of the Q1 guide sits below Q4'26 revenue' is argued in both growth.points[5] and scenarioCommentary. The sensitivity is restated in full in finalRecommendation.body[0] after scenarioCommentary sets it out.
findings.fix: Argue the unlabelled-EPS caveat once, in multiplesCommentary where the earnings anchor is introduced. The Base driver, scenarioCommentary and the thesis can refer to it in a few words ('the unlabelled EPS anchor above'). The final recommendation can name it as a reason without re-explaining it. Have scenarioCommentary point to the growth section for the Q1 guide and the unmanned result rather than restating them, and have the final recommendation point to the sensitivity rather than listing both changes again.
findings.note: Resolved. The unlabelled-EPS caveat is argued once, in multiplesCommentary. The thesis, Base driver and scenarioCommentary point to it in a few words, and the final recommendation names it as a reason without re-explaining it. scenarioCommentary points to the growth section for the Q1 guide and the unmanned result, and the final recommendation points to the sensitivity.

findings.quote: Software and services include out-of-band management, GPS-based vehicle and asset tracking, engineering services, and extended warranty and support.
findings.issue: The company description lists these offerings ('In addition, the company offers single-pane-of-glass management for out-of-band (OOB)… GPS-based vehicle and asset tracking… engineering services… extended warranty, support, and maintenance services') but never assigns them to the Software and Services product line. Mapping them into that line is an inference the surface does not make.
findings.fix: List them as further offerings, as the description does, for example 'The company also offers…', without assigning them to the Software and Services product line.
findings.note: Resolved. companyOverview now reads 'The company also offers out-of-band management, GPS-based vehicle and asset tracking…' without assigning those offerings to the Software and Services line.

findings.quote: it funds the Vecima acquisition, closed on August 1, 2026, without borrowing, and leaves room to absorb a slower year.
findings.issue: The pack does not say how the acquisition was paid for. The MD&A gives 'aggregate consideration of approximately $11.7 million' and the closing date, nothing more. 'Funds the Vecima acquisition… without borrowing' (balanceCommentary) and 'the company used about $11.7 million… to buy' (capitalAllocation) state the cash funding as fact. The previous draft correctly said the balance sheet gives room to fund it.
findings.fix: Restore the hedge: the year-end cash and no-debt position gives the company room to fund the approximately $11.7 million consideration without borrowing. In capitalAllocation, describe the $11.7 million as the aggregate consideration rather than cash used.
findings.note: Resolved. balanceCommentary restores the hedge ('gives the company room to fund the Vecima consideration… without borrowing'). capitalAllocation describes the July 2026 agreement and the 'aggregate consideration of approximately $11.7 million', with the August 1, 2026 close, matching the MD&A.

findings.quote: the fourth quarter of FY26 extended a run of sequential revenue growth and gross margin rose, while the annual GAAP result remained a loss
findings.issue: The sentence reads as though gross margin rose in the fourth quarter, but the page carries no quarterly gross margin. The 43.8% versus 42.1% gain is annual. That also cuts against the sentence's own frame, 'shows in the quarters but not yet in the full year', since the gross-margin gain is visible in the full year.
findings.fix: Attribute the gross-margin gain to FY26 (the full year), or drop it from this sentence. Keep the quarter-versus-full-year contrast to revenue growth and the GAAP loss.
findings.note: Resolved. The gross-margin clause is dropped from analystCommentary; the quarter-versus-full-year contrast now covers only sequential revenue growth and the annual GAAP loss.
